original_question: In the spaces Rat_d and Poly_d of rational and polynomial maps of degree d with the topology of uniform convergence, is the subset of expanding maps dense? Equivalently, is every rational or polynomial map approximable by maps for which some iterate uniformly expands the spherical metric on the Julia set?
target_in_paper: §5, "Geometrically finite maps and Kleinian groups" (McMullen), under "Geometrically finite rational maps": the unnumbered Conjecture that the expanding maps are dense in Rat_d and Poly_d.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the paper's exact target very closely: it asks about density in Rat_d and Poly_d, keeps the topology of uniform convergence, and uses the paper's explicit equivalent reformulation that an expanding map is one for which some iterate uniformly expands the spherical metric on the Julia set.
missing_details: State that d is fixed, so the density question is asked separately inside each space Rat_d and Poly_d of degree-d maps.
Specify the ambient setting: rational maps are self-maps of the Riemann sphere, and polynomial maps are degree-d complex polynomials viewed as rational maps.
Define "expanding" exactly as the paper does: if C is the set of critical points, P = ∪_{n≥1} f^n(C) is the post-critical set, and J(f) is the Julia set, then f is expanding when P ∩ J(f) = ∅.
Make the quantifier in the equivalent formulation explicit: for each approximating map g, there exists some iterate g^n, with n depending on g, that uniformly expands the spherical metric on J(g).
Clarify that approximation is taken within the same space Rat_d or Poly_d, with the topology of uniform convergence.
Optionally note the paper's terminology that these expanding maps are also called hyperbolic or Axiom A maps.
refined_question: For a fixed degree d, let Rat_d be the space of degree-d rational self-maps of the Riemann sphere and Poly_d the space of degree-d complex polynomials, each equipped with the topology of uniform convergence. If, for a map f, C(f) denotes its set of critical points, P(f) = ∪_{n≥1} f^n(C(f)) its post-critical set, and J(f) its Julia set, and if f is called expanding when P(f) ∩ J(f) = ∅ (equivalently, when some iterate f^n uniformly expands the spherical metric on J(f)), is the set of expanding maps dense in Rat_d and in Poly_d?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, for each fixed d, are the hyperbolic (Axiom A) maps dense in Rat_d and in Poly_d?
justification: The draft is essentially the paper's exact unnumbered Conjecture in §5. In the paragraph immediately preceding the conjecture, the paper defines an expanding rational map by the condition P ∩ J = ∅, where C is the critical set and P = ∪_{n≥1} f^n(C) is the post-critical set, and states that this is equivalent to the existence of an iterate that uniformly expands the spherical metric on the Julia set; it also says these maps are called hyperbolic or Axiom A. The conjecture then asks whether the expanding maps are dense in Rat_d and Poly_d, with those spaces equipped with the topology of uniform convergence. The only substantive omissions in the draft are the paper's exact definition of expanding, the explicit notation C, P, and J, the fact that d is fixed, and the ambient sphere setting. Also, this paper is a short problem list, so there is no numbered Conjecture 1.1, Proposition 1.2, or Theorem 1.3 to invoke instead.
